summary: Shichang Ma was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology who taught Giuseppe Vignato. He held posts as a Buddhist archaeology researcher at Dunhuang Academy (1963–1978) and in the Archaeology Department at Peking University (1982).
Shigeki Kudo is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held posts as an assistant at Kyoto University and as an associate professor at Shuchiin University and Shitennoji University (attested 1972–1973).

Shigeo Kamata studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo (~1953–1958). A scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology, he held appointments at the University of Tokyo (~1958–1988), Aichi Gakuin University (~1988–1996), and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Shigeru Gorai studied at Kyoto University and the University of Tokyo (~1928–1931). Specializing in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology, he held posts at Ryukoku University (attested 1962), Otani University (~1960–1974), and Koyasan University (~1974–1988).

Shigeru Matsumoto studied at the University of Tokyo (~1952–1960) and Harvard University (~1961–1967). Working in religious studies, he held academic positions at Tenri University (~1967–1985) and the University of the Sacred Heart (~1985–2004).
Shigetsu Sasaki studied at Tokyo Academy of Fine Arts (~1902–1906) and under Sokatsu Shaku (~1905–1919). Active in Buddhist studies, he founded the First Zen Institute of America in 1931.

Shili Xiong was a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied at China Inner Learning College in 1920. He held a post at Peking University from 1923 to 1955 and taught Junyi Tang and Zongsan Mou.

Shin Fujinaga is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He was affiliated with Hiroshima University (attested 1992) and served as an associate professor at the National Institute of Technology, Miyakonojo College (attested 1998–2000).
Shin Kitada completed doctoral studies at the University of Halle-Wittenberg in Indology. Kitada was affiliated with the Eastern Institute (attested 2008–2010).

Shin'ichi Hisamatsu studied at Kyoto University (~1912–1915) under Kitaro Nishida and Shozan Ikegami. A scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy, he held posts at Ryukoku University, Kyoto University, Hanazono University, and Harvard, and founded Gakudō Dōjō.

Shin'ichi Yoshinaga studied at Kyoto University (~1976–1981). Working in religious studies and Buddhist studies, he held a post at the National Institute of Technology, Maizuru College from ~1988 to 2017.
Shindai Sekiguchi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University (~1926–1931). He later served as a professor at Taisho University (~1960–1978) and Hanazono University (~1978–1983).

Shingen Takagi studied at Tohoku University under scholars including Gisho Nakano, Yusho Miyasaka, Ensho Kanakura, and Hakuyu Hadano. A scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies, he served at Koyasan University as an associate professor (attested 1970) and president (attested 1991–1995).

Shingo Einoo completed a PhD in Indology under Wilhelm Rau at the University of Marburg (~1975–1982). He held an assistant post at the National Museum of Ethnology (~1985–1989) and taught Kei Kataoka.

Shinichi Tsuda studied under Akira Hirakawa at the University of Tokyo and earned a Ph.D. under Jan Willem de Jong and Arthur Llewellyn Basham at ANU. Specializing in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, he held posts at Eastern Institute and ICPBS.
Shinjo Hinonishi worked in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Japanology. He served at Koyasan University as an associate professor (attested 1980) and professor (attested 2008).

Shinjo Kawasaki studied under Hajime Nakamura and at Columbia University, among other teachers. In Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, he held posts at Toyo Bunko (~1960–1975), University of Tsukuba (1975), and Taisho University (~2005–2011).

Shinjo Suguro studied at the University of Tokyo (~1945–1948, Litt.D. 1987). Specializing in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy, he served as vice director (1980) and professor emeritus (attested 2009) at Rissho University.
Shinkai Sugawara was a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied at Waseda University (~1949–1957). He later held an academic post at Waseda University from ~1964 to 1996.

Shinkan Murakami earned his doctorates at Tohoku University, studying under Ensho Kanakura, Ryujo Yamada, and Hakuyu Hadano. A scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, he held posts at Tohoku University and Seiwa Gakuen College (~1996–2007).
